problemStatement.formal: \lambda(n) = \operatorname{exponent}((\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^*) and, for every unit a, a^{\lambda(n)} = 1; moreover \lambda(n) divides \varphi(n), is minimal among universal exponents, and \lambda(p)=p-1 for prime p.
problemStatement.plain: Define Carmichael's function as the exponent of the unit group modulo n, then prove its universal-exponent, divisibility, minimality, and prime-modulus properties.
whyMatters: Carmichael's function is the exact universal exponent behind modular arithmetic and RSA-style correctness conditions.
The proof shows these facts are direct consequences of Mathlib's abstract group exponent API.

proven: carmichael_pow_eq_one proves the universal exponent property for every unit.
carmichael_dvd_totient proves lambda(n) divides Nat.totient n.
carmichael_minimal proves any universal exponent is a multiple of lambda(n).
carmichael_prime proves lambda(p)=p-1 for prime p; carmichael_one and carmichael_two prove the small cases.
